screens.module: M0: Why We're Here: Your Floor, Your Numbers
screens.title: Welcome: Your Floor, Your Calls
screens.on_screen_text:
Forklift Safety Refresher: Inspect, Yield, Stay Stable

Last year's near misses: mostly pedestrians at intersections and dock doors, plus a couple of raised-load turns.
Also: pre-shift checks sometimes signed, not done.
[CLIENT TO CONFIRM: real figures, if approved]

About 24 minutes. Your place is saved.
[Start]
screens.narration: You're certified, and many of you have run trucks on these floors for years, so this isn't a rules lecture. It's about the quick calls you make on a busy shift. Last year, most near misses across our three DCs were pedestrian conflicts at intersections and dock doors, plus a couple of tip-over scares from turning with a raised load. And pre-shift checks sometimes get signed without being done. Over the next 24 minutes, you'll make those calls yourself.
screens.visuals: Full-bleed real video loop (10 to 15 seconds, muted, no flashing) or still photo: a counterbalance truck traveling a DC aisle at shift start, operator in correct PPE, a reach truck working at height in the background. Title and text are live Storyline text on a dark semi-opaque panel (contrast at least 4.5:1). As the narration reaches 'Last year', three realistic photo tiles fade in along the bottom, each with a live-text label: (1) 'Pedestrians at intersections and dock doors': a pedestrian stepping out at a racking end cap as a truck approaches; (2) 'Raised-load turns': a counterbalance truck turning at an aisle end with a pallet at chest height; (3) 'Checks signed, not done': an operator ticking a checklist without leaving the seat. If the client approves real figures, add a simple bar chart built from live Storyline shapes and text, with a data table equivalent. Client logo top left [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: logo file]. Use footage from the client's DCs if a shoot is approved, otherwise realistic stock that matches the fleet.
screens.interaction: Learner selects Start (mouse, or Tab then Enter or Space). Start jumps to M0-S03. On return visits, the course resumes automatically at the last screen viewed (Resume set to Always resume), with no prompt. The background video loop has a visible Pause button (WCAG 2.2.2).
screens.feedback: None.

screens.module: M0: Why We're Here: Your Floor, Your Numbers
screens.title: Your Route Through the Course
screens.on_screen_text:
Your route:
1. The Pre-Shift Inspection That Actually Counts (6 min)
2. Intersections and Dock Doors: Seeing People First (6 min)
3. Loads, Turns and Tip-Overs (6 min)
4. Final Check (about 5 min)

Stopping early? Your place is saved.
screens.narration: Three parts of about six minutes each, then a short final check. They open in order the first time through. If your huddle runs short, close the course; it picks up where you left off. Captions are on because the floor is loud, and the CC button turns them off. Let's start where every shift starts: with the truck.
screens.visuals: Course menu with four large tiles. Each tile has a realistic photo thumbnail (truck inspection, intersection, raised load, operator at a terminal), a live-text title and the duration. Tile states: Available (no icon), Locked (padlock icon plus the word 'Locked'), Done (check icon plus the word 'Done'). Tile 4 has two extra states: Passed (check icon plus the word 'Passed') and Attempts used (information icon plus the words 'Attempts used').
screens.interaction:
Hub menu. Learner selects the Module 1 tile. On first attempt, tiles 2 to 4 are locked. Tile 2 unlocks when M1_Done is true, tile 3 when M2_Done is true, and tile 4 when M1_Done, M2_Done and M3_Done are all true. Modules 1 to 3 stay open for review once done. Each module's summary screen returns to this hub.
TILE 4 (FINAL CHECK) ROUTING, triggers in this order:
1) Jump to M4-S23 if M4_Passed = true OR Attempts >= 3. (A learner who has passed, or used all attempts, gets the wrap-up and quick reference, never a new scored attempt.)
2) Jump to M4-S01 if M4_Passed = false AND Attempts < 3 AND the tile is unlocked.
TILE 4 STATE on timeline start: Passed if M4_Passed = true; Attempts used if M4_Passed = false and Attempts >= 3; otherwise Available or Locked as above.
screens.feedback: If a locked tile is selected: 'This part opens after you finish the one before it.'
screens.notes:
Tiles are buttons with accessible names that include their state, for example 'Module 2, Intersections and Dock Doors, 6 minutes, locked' or 'Final Check, passed'. Locked tiles stay in the tab order so screen reader users hear the locked state. Thumbnails are decorative (the tile text carries the meaning).
This hub is the only entry in the player Menu (global note 1).

screens.module: M1: The Pre-Shift Inspection That Actually Counts
screens.title: Same Truck, Two Checks
screens.on_screen_text:
Same truck. Two checks.
Look, touch, test.

One-minute check: 0 defects found
Real check: 3 defects found
screens.narration: Most defects don't show from the seat. Here's truck 07, checked two ways. On the left, the one-minute version: glance at the gauges, tick, sign. Every box says OK. On the right, the same truck, checked on foot. Wear at the heel of the left fork, with a fine crack starting. Hydraulic fluid under the mast. Then the tests: horn fine, reverse alarm silent. Each one takes away a margin you rely on: fork strength, lift control, and the warning people listen for.
screens.visuals: Worked-example video or animated photo sequence (about 40 seconds), split screen. LEFT, live-text label 'One-minute check': Marcus seated, glancing at the display, ticking boxes, signing. RIGHT, live-text label 'Real check': Marcus walking around truck 07; close-ups of (1) left fork heel wear with a fine crack, (2) fluid drips and a wet patch under the mast, (3) Marcus selecting reverse with no alarm. Each defect is marked as the narration names it by a double-stroke outline (white inner line, dark outer line) with a numbered live-text label, so the marker reaches at least 3:1 contrast on light floors and yellow trucks and never relies on color alone. Counters '0 defects found' and '3 defects found' are live text. No text burned into the video.
screens.interaction: Video with player play, pause and replay. Next is enabled at all times.
screens.feedback: None.
screens.notes:
Revision 3: narration trimmed from about 100 to about 82 words; video shortened to about 40 seconds; outlines changed to a double stroke (WCAG 1.4.11).
CAPTIONS include sound descriptions: [horn sounds] and [reverse selected, no alarm sound].
ALT TEXT (poster frame): 'Split screen of the same forklift: on the left, an operator ticks a checklist from the seat; on the right, the operator inspects the forks, mast and reverse alarm on foot.'
The narration describes each defect as it appears, so it doubles as audio description.
SME TO VERIFY: Dana to confirm the three defects match the client checklist and are realistic for the fleet. Fork heel wear limits come from the SOP or manufacturer; no figures on screen.

screens.module: M1: The Pre-Shift Inspection That Actually Counts
screens.title: Easy to Skip, Expensive to Miss
screens.on_screen_text:
Easy to skip. Expensive to miss.
Select any item to see why it matters.

[Forks] [Chains] [Hydraulics] [Tires] [Horn, lights, reverse or travel alarm] [Brakes] [Seatbelt or restraint] [Data plate] [Battery or LPG] [Reach truck extras]
screens.narration: These are the items that get skipped most. Know them cold? Move on. Newer? Select a few to see why each one is on your checklist.
screens.visuals: Photo of a counterbalance truck with numbered marker shapes (double stroke, global note 5) on each area, matching the numbered buttons. Each reveal layer shows a close-up photo of that item plus live text. The 'Reach truck extras' layer shows a reach truck close-up (baselegs, load wheels, operator presence pedal).
screens.interaction:
Optional click-to-reveal with 10 buttons, each opening a layer with a close-up photo and text. Viewed buttons show a check icon plus the word 'Viewed'. Next is always enabled (optional exploration).
LAYER TEXT:
Forks: 'Look for cracks, bends and heel wear, and check the locking pins. A worn heel can fail under a load you've lifted a hundred times.'
Chains: 'Check for stretch, kinks, rust and uneven tension. If a chain fails, the carriage drops, along with whatever is on it.'
Hydraulics: 'Look for leaks at hoses, fittings and cylinders, and for fluid under the mast. A leak can mean a load that drifts down or a lift that fails.'
Tires: 'Check for chunks, cuts, flat spots and wear (and pressure on pneumatic tires). Damaged tires reduce stability, especially in turns.'
Horn, lights, reverse or travel alarm: 'Test them, don't assume. The horn, the lights and the reverse alarm (counterbalance) or travel alarm (reach truck) are how pedestrians know you're there.'
Brakes: 'Test the service and parking brakes before you lift anything. You need them most when you're loaded.'
Seatbelt or restraint: 'Check that it latches and isn't cut or frayed. On a sit-down truck, it keeps you inside the overhead guard in a tip-over.'
Data plate: 'It must be present and readable. It's how you know the rated capacity and load center.'
Battery or LPG: 'Electric: cables and connectors undamaged, no corrosion. LPG: cylinder secure, connection tight, no smell of gas.' [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: checklist wording]
Reach truck extras: 'Also check the reach mechanism, the load wheels in the baselegs, and the operator presence pedal.' [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: from the reach truck checklist]
screens.feedback: None (informational reveals).
screens.notes:
Revision 3: alarm label standardized to the glossary terms (global note 14); narration trimmed.
FINAL ITEM LIST must match the client's pre-shift checklist(s) [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: separate checklists for counterbalance and reach, electric and LPG?]. Dana to verify every reason statement.
Each layer has a Close button. Focus goes to the layer heading on open and back to the button on close. Each button's accessible name includes its viewed state.
ALT TEXT base photo: 'Counterbalance forklift with numbered markers on the forks, chains, mast hoses, tires, horn and lights, brakes, seatbelt, data plate and LPG cylinder.' Close-up alt text describes each item, for example 'Close-up of a fork heel showing wear.'
First item on the alpha cut list (global note 12).

screens.module: M1: The Pre-Shift Inspection That Actually Counts
screens.title: Inspect Truck 07 (Counterbalance)
screens.on_screen_text:
Inspect truck 07.
Select each item to inspect it, then choose OK or Flag as defect.
Select Done when you'd sign off.

Items flagged: %M1_Flagged%
[Checklist view]  [Done]
screens.narration: Truck 07. Walk-around first, then the operational tests. Select each item, inspect it, then decide: OK, or flag it.
screens.visuals: High-resolution photo or 3D render of a sit-down counterbalance truck (LPG or electric to match the fleet [CLIENT TO CONFIRM]), three-quarter view. 8 inspectable items in walk-around order: 4 planted defects (1 left fork heel wear with a hairline crack; 3 fluid weeping at the lift cylinder hose fitting with a wet patch under the mast; 5 seatbelt buckle that won't latch; 7 silent reverse alarm) and 4 normal items with harmless cosmetic wear so the learner has to judge (2 chains with surface grime; 4 tires with light sidewall scuffing; 6 LPG cylinder with dust; 8 brakes). Operational tests sit on a dashboard inset: Test reverse alarm, Test brakes. Each inspect layer shows a close-up image or plays the test, plus a live-text description. Hotspot focus and state markers use the double stroke (global note 5).
screens.interaction:
INSPECT FLOW (same logic in hotspot view and Checklist view):
1) Selecting an item opens its Inspect layer: close-up image (or test sound or silence) plus the description below. Nothing on this layer says whether the item is OK.
2) Two buttons: [OK] and [Flag as defect]. The learner must choose one.
3) Only after the choice does the one-sentence feedback appear, with a Close button. The choice is then locked. The hotspot changes state: 'OK' (check icon plus the word OK) or 'Flagged' (flag icon plus the word Flagged).
4) Flag on a defect: add 1 to M1_Found and M1_Flagged. Flag on a normal item: add 1 to M1_FalseFlags and M1_Flagged. OK on a defect: the hotspot also gets a hidden 'Missed' state used by the results layer.
5) Done is available at any time. Items never inspected count as not inspected; defects among them appear on the results layer as 'Not inspected'.
CHECKLIST VIEW (accessible alternative, same variables and states): a list of the 8 items in walk-around order. Each item shows its description and two radio buttons (OK, Flag as defect); the feedback appears under the item after a choice.
INSPECT DESCRIPTIONS:
1 Forks: 'Left fork: heel worn, with a fine line across the bend. Right fork: no damage.'
2 Chains: 'Even tension, links lubricated, no kinks. Grime on the outer plates.'
3 Mast and hoses: 'Fluid weeping at the lift cylinder hose fitting. Wet patch on the floor below.'

screens.module: M1: The Pre-Shift Inspection That Actually Counts
screens.title: Operate, Report or Tag Out
screens.on_screen_text:
Every check ends one of three ways:
- Passes: operate.
- Minor, no safety impact: operate and report.
- Affects safe operation: tag out, report, don't operate.
Not sure? Tag it out and ask.

OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178: examine before use, at least daily. Site SOP [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section]
screens.narration: Every check ends one of three ways. Everything passes: you operate. Something minor that doesn't affect safe operation, like [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: example, for instance a torn seat cover]: operate and report it. Anything that affects how the truck lifts, steers, stops, warns people or protects you: tag it, report it to [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: supervisor or maintenance contact], and don't drive it. OSHA requires that check before use, at least daily, and an unsafe truck stays out of service until it's repaired.
screens.visuals: Three-column decision graphic in live text, each column marked by a different shape icon plus a label: a check mark ('Operate'), a clipboard ('Operate and report'), a tag ('Tag out'). Under the Tag out column, a photo of the client's out-of-service tag [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: tag design]. Sources line in smaller text at the bottom (still at least 4.5:1 contrast).
screens.interaction: None. Learner selects Next.
screens.feedback: None.
screens.notes:
Revision 3: narration trimmed from about 110 to about 78 words. The OSHA lead-in and the spoken 'Not sure? Tag it out and ask' were cut; the OSHA basis is now one closing sentence and the 'not sure' rule stays on screen.
SME TO VERIFY: wording reflects 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (examined before being placed in service, at least daily; after each shift where trucks are used round the clock) and 1910.178(q)(1) (trucks not in safe operating condition removed from service). The three categories, the minor-defect example, the reporting contact, the tag-out steps (for example tag on the controls, key removed, maintenance notified) and the 'when in doubt, tag it out' guidance must all come from the site SOP [CLIENT TO CONFIRM].
ALT TEXT for the tag photo: 'The site's out-of-service tag.' Columns are built as a three-item list for screen readers.

screens.on_screen_text:
You're on truck 07 and your check finds a crack at the heel of the left fork.
The first trailer has waited 10 minutes. Priya's on the radio.
What do you do?

A) Operate, but keep loads light until maintenance can look at it.
B) Unload the first trailer, then tag it out and report it.
C) Tag it out now, report it and take another truck.
screens.narration:
Whichever truck you inspected, picture yourself on truck 07, with a crack at the fork heel.

VOICE B (Priya, on radio): Door 2's still waiting. You on your way?
screens.visuals: Close-up of the cracked fork heel (same asset as M1-S03), with a handheld radio clipped to the operator's vest in the foreground and the dock with a waiting trailer blurred in the background.

screens.feedback:
A (incorrect): 'You run light pallets for an hour. On the fourth, the fork tip catches the pallet deck and the cracked heel gives way. The load drops at the dock edge, a few feet from Luis. Nobody's hurt this time. A cracked fork isn't a defect you can drive carefully around. Try again.'
B (incorrect): 'You clear the trailer in 25 minutes, lifting every pallet on a cracked fork. Nothing breaks this time, but every lift was a gamble, and the tag came too late to protect anyone, including you. A tag-out defect comes out of service when you find it, not when it's convenient. Try again.'
C (correct): 'Right call. You tag truck 07 out of service [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: tag and key steps], report it to [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: contact], and take truck 09. You're eight minutes behind. Eight minutes is a lot cheaper than a dropped load.'
screens.notes:
Revision 3 (LO2 discrimination): option B is now a delayed tag-out, so the correct answer is no longer the only option that mentions tagging. The learner has to judge when, not just whether. Narration trimmed.
Consequence layers use a still image for each outcome (A: pallet dropped on the dock floor, no one hurt, Luis stepping back; B: the operator lifting a pallet at the trailer, with a close-up inset of the cracked heel; C: tag hanging on the steering wheel). Non-graphic.

screens.title: The Approach Sequence
screens.on_screen_text:
Every intersection. Every dock door.
1. Slow down
2. Sound the horn
3. Look both ways
4. Yield to pedestrians
5. Make eye contact
6. Proceed

Look both ways. Yield to pedestrians: at our sites, [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: pedestrians have the right of way]. Then get eye contact. The horn tells people you're there. Eye contact tells you they know. No eye contact? Stop and wait. Then proceed.

screens.module: M3: Loads, Turns and Tip-Overs
screens.title: The Stability Triangle
screens.on_screen_text:
The stability triangle:
- Three points: two front wheels and the steer axle pivot
- Truck + load = one combined center of gravity
- Inside the triangle: upright
- Higher load, faster, tighter turn: closer to the edge
screens.narration: Most counterbalance trucks rest on three points: the two front wheels and the pivot in the middle of the steer axle. That's the stability triangle. Truck and load share one combined center of gravity, and while it stays inside the triangle, you stay upright. Raise the load and that point climbs, so it takes less to push it sideways. A turn pushes it out; speed and rough floor push harder. Past the edge, the truck goes over. Reach trucks have a different base, but the rule is the same.
screens.visuals: Animated diagram, synced to the narration: top-down truck outline with the stability triangle drawn as a bold dashed outline, and the combined center of gravity as a circle marker with the live-text label 'CG'. A side view shows the CG rising as the load rises. In the turn, the CG marker slides toward the triangle edge, with an arrow and live-text label 'Turn'. When it crosses, the edge outline thickens and the live-text label 'Outside: tip-over' appears. Plain-language labels only, no formulas, no text baked into the animation.
screens.interaction: Animation with play, pause and replay. Next enabled.
screens.feedback: None.

screens.on_screen_text:

screens.narration: Now try it. Change the load height, speed and turn, and watch the center of gravity. Find what takes it over the edge, then what keeps it centered.
screens.visuals: Same top-down triangle diagram as M3-S02, with the CG marker moving to one of three positions: center (Stable), near the edge (Reduced margin) or outside (Tip-over). A side-view truck shows the load at the selected height. Three rows of segmented buttons for the settings. The result panel sits directly beneath the settings on the base slide: a headline with an icon per state (circle = Stable, triangle with exclamation mark = Reduced margin, crossed circle = Tip-over) and up to two factor lines below it, all live text.
screens.interaction:
Three button sets (radio-style, one selected per set). Default: Floor, Walking, Gentle. Every change updates the result immediately. Sim_Tries adds 1 per change; Next enables after 3 changes.
RESULT PANEL BUILD (revision 3): the result is on the BASE SLIDE, not a layer. The headline is one text box with four states (STABLE-1, STABLE-2, REDUCED, TIP-OVER); each factor line is a text box shown or hidden by its condition. A change of setting only changes these states. FOCUS STAYS ON THE BUTTON JUST SELECTED: no trigger moves focus and no layer opens (WCAG 3.2.2 On Input).
FOCUS ORDER: title, instruction line ('After each change, the result appears below the settings.'), Load height set, Speed set, Turn set, result headline, factor lines, diagram (alt text), Next. So the result is always the next thing after the settings for keyboard and screen reader users.
RESULT LOGIC (Dana to approve). Conditions use the selected state of each button, not extra variables.
FLOOR (travel height): Walking + Gentle = STABLE-1; Moderate + Gentle = STABLE-1; Walking + Tight = STABLE-2; Moderate + Tight = REDUCED; Fast + Gentle = REDUCED; Fast + Tight = TIP-OVER.
KNEE: Walking + Gentle = REDUCED; Walking + Tight = REDUCED; Moderate + Gentle = REDUCED; Moderate + Tight = REDUCED; Fast + Gentle = TIP-OVER; Fast + Tight = TIP-OVER.
CHEST: Walking + Gentle = REDUCED; Walking + Tight = REDUCED; Moderate + Gentle = REDUCED; Moderate + Tight = TIP-OVER; Fast + Gentle = TIP-OVER; Fast + Tight = TIP-OVER.
OVERHEAD: Walking + Gentle = REDUCED; every other combination = TIP-OVER.
Rules this table enforces: any height above Floor is never Stable; 'how you want to travel' appears only for Floor with Walking or Moderate and a Gentle turn; Fast into a Tight turn is always Tip-over.
FACTOR LINES (each text box shown only when its condition is true, stacked under the headline):
F-HEIGHT (Knee, Chest or Overhead; one state per height)
F-FAST (Speed = Fast; one state for Gentle, one for Tight)
F-MODTIGHT (Speed = Moderate and Turn = Tight)
screens.feedback:
HEADLINES:
STABLE-1: 'Stable. Load at travel height, controlled speed, gentle turn. The center of gravity stays well inside the triangle. This is how you want to travel.'
STABLE-2: 'Stable. Load at travel height and walking speed, so the center of gravity stays inside the triangle, even in a tight turn.'
REDUCED: 'Reduced margin. The center of gravity is close to the edge of the triangle. A floor joint, a sudden steer or a bit more speed could push it over.'
TIP-OVER: 'Tip-over. The center of gravity has crossed the edge of the triangle, and the truck tips toward the outside of the turn.'
FACTOR LINES:
F-HEIGHT: 'Load raised to knee height.' / 'Load raised to chest height.' / 'Load raised overhead.' Each followed by: 'Never travel with the load raised. Raise and lower only when stopped.'
F-FAST (Gentle): 'You're traveling fast. Get your speed down on the straight, before the turn.'
F-FAST (Tight): 'Fast into a tight turn. That can tip a truck even with the load at travel height. Slow down on the straight.'
F-MODTIGHT: 'Moderate speed into a tight turn. Slow to walking speed before a tight turn.'
screens.notes:
Revision 3 (QA major finding 5): the Result layer and its automatic focus move are removed. The result now updates in place on the base slide while focus stays on the selected button.
SLIDE PROPERTY: When revisiting: Reset to initial state.

Diagram alt text updates with the state, for example 'Center of gravity marker is outside the stability triangle.'

screens.title: If It Starts to Tip
screens.on_screen_text:
If it starts to tip:

Sit-down counterbalance:
- Don't jump
- Stay in the seat, belt on
- Grip the wheel, brace your feet
- Lean away from the fall

Reach truck: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: SOP response for the fleet's reach truck models]

FALLBACK TEXT if not confirmed by script lock: 'Reach truck: follow the tip-over response in your SOP and your truck's operator's manual. Your supervisor will review it with you.'
screens.narration:

screens.on_screen_text:
You need to move a tall stack of empty totes across the dock staging area. The stack blocks your view ahead. What do you do?

A) Travel forward, leaning out to check around the stack
B) Travel with the load trailing, looking the way you're going
C) Travel forward slowly; people will see a load that big
D) Raise the stack until you can see under it
screens.visuals: Operator's view with a tall stack of totes blocking most of the forward view, and the dock staging area beyond.
screens.interaction: Single choice, scored. CORRECT ANSWER: B. Shuffle on.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The answer is: travel with the load trailing, looking the way you're going, then slow down and sound the horn at the crossing. Leaning out puts you outside the overhead guard, relying on others to see you is an assumption, and raising the load raises the center of gravity. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
Option D also reinforces LO5 (raised load).
ALT TEXT: 'Operator's view: a tall stack of totes blocks the view ahead toward the dock staging area.'
Est. time: 0:25.

screens.module: M4: Final Check: Your Shift, Your Calls
screens.title: Bank LO5, Item 1: Why a Raised Load Tips
screens.on_screen_text:
Why is turning with a raised load more likely to cause a tip-over than turning with the load low?

A) Raising the load moves the center of gravity forward, so the truck tips forward in the turn
B) Raising the load lifts the combined center of gravity, so the turn can push it outside the triangle more easily
C) Raising the load takes weight off the front wheels, so they lose grip and slide in the turn
D) Raising the load moves the center of gravity toward the counterweight, so the rear swings out
screens.visuals: Side-view diagram of a counterbalance truck with the load raised and the combined CG marker shown high (live-text label 'CG').
screens.interaction: Single choice, scored. CORRECT ANSWER: B. Shuffle on.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The answer is: raising the load lifts the combined center of gravity, so the turn can push it outside the triangle more easily. Raising the load doesn't shift the center of gravity forward or back, or change grip at the wheels. The higher it is, the less sideways force it takes to push it past the edge. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
SME TO VERIFY: distractors A, C and D are clearly incorrect as explanations for lateral tip-over.
ALT TEXT: 'Side view of a forklift with the load raised and the combined center of gravity marked high above the truck.'
Est. time: 0:25.

screens.module: M4: Final Check: Your Shift, Your Calls
screens.title: Bank LO5, Item 2: Closest to the Edge
screens.on_screen_text:
Which combination moves the combined center of gravity closest to the edge of the stability triangle?

A) Load low, slow speed, gentle turn
B) Load low, moderate speed, traveling straight
C) Load raised, moderate speed, tight turn
D) No load, slow speed, gentle turn
screens.visuals: Top-down stability triangle diagram with the CG marker at the center (no answer shown).
screens.interaction: Single choice, scored. CORRECT ANSWER: C. Shuffle on.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The answer is: load raised, moderate speed, tight turn. Height, speed and a tight turn each push the center of gravity toward the edge, and together they add up fast. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
ALT TEXT: 'Top-down diagram of the stability triangle with the center of gravity marker in the middle.'
Est. time: 0:20.

screens.module: M4: Final Check: Your Shift, Your Calls
screens.title: Bank LO5, Item 3: Ray's Wheel Lift
screens.on_screen_text:
On nights, Ray's counterbalance truck lifts a wheel turning out of aisle 30. Which factors pushed the center of gravity toward the edge? Select all that apply.

[ ] A) The pallet was raised to shoulder height
[ ] B) He held his speed into the turn
[ ] C) He steered sharply at the aisle end
[ ] D) The mast was tilted back
[ ] E) The load was centered on the forks
screens.visuals: Still: a counterbalance truck leaning in a turn at the end of an aisle at night, one wheel just off the floor, pallet at shoulder height. Non-graphic. Aisle number repeated in live text. No letter labels on the image.
screens.interaction: Multiple response, scored, all-or-nothing. CORRECT ANSWERS: raised pallet, held speed, sharp steer (A, B, C in this storyboard). Shuffle on (no lettered image), so the correct answers appear in varying positions.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The factors were the pallet raised to shoulder height, speed held into the turn and a sharp steer at the aisle end. Each moves the center of gravity toward the edge, and together they lifted the wheel. A mast tilted back and a load centered on the forks are safe practices. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
Revision 3: shuffle turned on and Why text written without letters, so the correct set no longer sits in a fixed A, B, C pattern.
ALT TEXT: 'Forklift with a pallet at shoulder height leaning in a turn at an aisle end, one wheel off the floor.'
Est. time: 0:30.

screens.module: M4: Final Check: Your Shift, Your Calls
screens.title: Bank LO6, Item 1: Off the Block Stack
screens.on_screen_text:
You've lifted a pallet off the top of a two-high block stack and backed out just far enough to clear it. The forks are at head height. What next?

A) Start toward the dock and lower gradually as you go
B) Stay stopped, lower to travel height and tilt back, then drive off
C) Drive at walking pace with it up, since it's a short trip
D) Keep it up until the turn, then lower before turning
screens.visuals: Photo of a counterbalance truck in a bulk storage area, forks at head height holding a pallet just lifted off a two-high block stack.
screens.interaction: Single choice, scored. CORRECT ANSWER: B. Shuffle on.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The answer is: stay stopped, lower to travel height and tilt back, then drive off. Raise and lower only when you're stopped, and never travel with the load up, even slowly or for a short trip. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
ALT TEXT: 'Forklift with its forks at head height holding a pallet just lifted from a two-high block stack.'
Est. time: 0:25.

screens.module: M4: Final Check: Your Shift, Your Calls
screens.title: Bank LO6, Item 2: When to Slow Down
screens.on_screen_text:
You're carrying a pallet down aisle 18 toward a right turn onto the main travel lane. When should you slow down?

A) In the turn, braking as you steer
B) Before the turn, while you're still traveling straight
C) After the turn, once you can see the lane
D) Only if there are pedestrians in the lane
screens.visuals: Operator's view along aisle 18 toward the aisle end and the main travel lane, with the load carried low.
screens.interaction: Single choice, scored. CORRECT ANSWER: B. Shuffle on.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The answer is: before the turn, while you're still traveling straight. Get your speed off on the straight so the turn needs no extra braking. Braking in the turn throws the load forward while the turn pushes it sideways. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
ALT TEXT: 'Operator's view of the end of aisle 18 ahead, with the load carried low.'
Est. time: 0:20.

screens.module: M4: Final Check: Your Shift, Your Calls
screens.title: Bank LO6, Item 3: Heavy, Long Load
screens.on_screen_text:
You're asked to move a pallet that looks heavier and longer than usual. Before you lift it, which check tells you whether your truck can safely carry it?

A) The rated capacity at that load center, as shown on the data plate
B) Whether the truck can lift it off the floor
C) Whether it looks balanced from the seat
D) Whether the last operator moved one like it
screens.visuals: Photo of an oversized, long pallet load on the floor with a counterbalance truck approaching.
screens.interaction: Single choice, scored. CORRECT ANSWER: A. Shuffle on.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The answer is the rated capacity at that load center, as shown on the data plate. A longer load moves the center of gravity forward and lowers what the truck can safely carry. A truck can lift a load it can't carry safely, and how a load looks doesn't tell you its weight or load center. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
SME TO VERIFY: the load center explanation. [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: what operators do when weight is unknown, for example ask a supervisor; add to the Why text if required.]
ALT TEXT: 'A long, heavy pallet load on the floor with a forklift approaching it.'
Est. time: 0:20.

screens.module: M4: Final Check: Your Shift, Your Calls
screens.title: Bank LO7, Item 1: Broken Floor in a Turn
screens.on_screen_text:
In a turn, a wheel drops into a broken section of floor and your sit-down counterbalance truck starts to go over to the left. You're belted in. What do you do?

A) Unbuckle and step off on the right as it goes
B) Stay seated and belted, hold the wheel, plant your feet and lean right
C) Reach out and grab the overhead guard post on the left
D) Brake hard to stop the truck before it goes over
screens.visuals: Still: sit-down counterbalance truck with a front wheel in a broken floor section, tilting left. Non-graphic.
screens.interaction: Single choice, scored. CORRECT ANSWER: B. Shuffle on. SAFETY-CRITICAL ITEM: tracked by M4-S22a if the must-pass rule is approved.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The answer is: stay seated and belted, hold the wheel, plant your feet and lean right, away from the fall. That keeps you inside the overhead guard. Operators who unbuckle, step off or reach out are often caught by the guard as the truck goes over, and braking won't stop a tip that's already started. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
Safety-critical item. Dana to verify.
ALT TEXT: 'Sit-down forklift with a front wheel in a broken section of floor, tilting to the left.'
Est. time: 0:25.

screens.module: M4: Final Check: Your Shift, Your Calls
screens.title: Bank LO7, Item 2: Not Belted In
screens.on_screen_text:
On a sit-down counterbalance truck, a turn goes wrong and the truck starts to tip. You realize you didn't fasten your seatbelt. What do you do?

A) Jump, since you're not held in anyway
B) Stay in the seat, grip the wheel, brace your feet and lean away from the fall
C) Grab the overhead guard with one hand outside the cab
D) Try to fasten the belt before it goes over
screens.visuals: Still: sit-down counterbalance truck mid-turn with the seatbelt visibly unfastened. Non-graphic.
screens.interaction: Single choice, scored. CORRECT ANSWER: B. Shuffle on. SAFETY-CRITICAL ITEM: tracked by M4-S22a if the must-pass rule is approved.
screens.feedback: WHY LAYER (review only; same text whatever the learner answered): 'The answer is: stay in the seat, grip the wheel, brace your feet and lean away from the fall. Even unbelted, the safest place is inside the overhead guard. Don't jump, don't put a hand outside the cab and don't fumble with the buckle. And always belt up before you move. SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'
screens.notes:
Safety-critical item. Dana to verify the guidance for an unbelted operator.
ALT TEXT: 'Sit-down forklift in a turn with the operator's seatbelt hanging unfastened.'
Est. time: 0:25.

screens.title: Bank LO7, Item 3 (Fallback): Load Shifts in a Turn
screens.on_screen_text:
You're turning a sit-down counterbalance truck when the load shifts sideways on the forks and the truck starts to tip to the right. You're belted in. What do you do?

A) Put your right foot out to steady the truck
B) Stay seated and belted, grip the wheel, brace your feet and lean left
C) Release the belt so you can jump clear to the left
D) Raise the forks to shift the weight back
screens.visuals: Still: sit-down counterbalance truck mid-turn, pallet slid toward the right fork, truck tilting right. Non-graphic.

SOP ref: [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: section].'

screens.on_screen_text:
PASS layer: 'You passed. Your score: %Results.ScorePercent%%. Review your answers to see the reason behind each one.' [Review answers] [Continue]

FAIL layer: 'Not this time. Your score: %Results.ScorePercent%%. You need 80% [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: and both safety-critical questions right]. Attempts left: %AttemptsLeft%.' [Review answers] [Back to menu] [Try again]

screens.narration:
PASS layer: You passed. Review your answers if you'd like the reasoning, then continue.

FAIL layer: Not this time. Review your answers, revisit any part from the menu, then try again with new questions.

FINAL FAIL layer: You've used all three attempts. [CLIENT TO CONFIRM: next step.] Continue to finish.
screens.visuals: Clean results panel with the score as live text. Pass: check icon plus the word 'Passed'. Fail and final fail: an information icon plus the words 'Not yet passed' (non-punitive tone). No red/green-only cues.
screens.interaction:
Storyline Results slide tracking all 10 drawn questions, pass at 80%. Settings: Allow user to review quiz; Show correct answers.
LAYER LOGIC (without must-pass): PASS if Results.ScorePercent >= 80. FAIL if Results.ScorePercent < 80 AND AttemptsLeft > 0. FINAL FAIL if Results.ScorePercent < 80 AND AttemptsLeft = 0.
LAYER LOGIC (with must-pass, only if approved): PASS if Results.ScorePercent >= 80 AND Results1.ScorePercent = 100 (Results1 is the hidden safety-critical results slide M4-S22a). FAIL or FINAL FAIL otherwise, split by AttemptsLeft as above. If Results.ScorePercent >= 80 but Results1.ScorePercent < 100, the FAIL or FINAL FAIL layer also shows: 'You scored %Results.ScorePercent%%, but one of the safety-critical questions (tag-out or tip-over) was wrong. Both must be right to pass.'

REVIEW ANSWERS: set ReviewMode = true, then Review Results. Each question shows Storyline's review marks plus its Why layer.
TRY AGAIN (FAIL layer only; shown when AttemptsLeft > 0): set ReviewMode = false, jump to M4-S01. Reset Results runs on Start there, so answers are always cleared and a new draw is made, whichever way the learner returns.

CONTINUE (PASS and FINAL FAIL layers): jump to M4-S23.

On a pass, the results slide reports passed with cmi.core.score.raw. When the FINAL FAIL layer opens, a Complete course trigger reports failed with the score [developer to confirm the exact trigger and status option in the current Storyline 360 update]. With must-pass approved, track using the M4-S22 results slide for score and triggers for status [developer to confirm the tracking option combination].
screens.feedback: See the layer text in on-screen text and narration. Item-level reasons are in each question's Why layer.
